answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned throughput caps: a fresh identity may move only tiny amounts at first, and its limit rises only after a long history of completed, dispute-free trades. Mass-producing fakes gains nothing, since each fake must patiently build the same slow history, like bees gathering nectar one trip at a time. Reputation is not a transferable relic: caps reset on ownership change, and a sudden volume jump from a quiet account hits a mesa-like plateau that holds until further honest activity proves it real.
